pairs.why: A keeps the real card's navy keys with cyan operator keys and a deep yellow-to-orange ground, while B swaps in cream keys and a paler, washed yellow glow.
A's water is a deeper blue and its sand a paler cream like the real card, while B's cyan is brighter and its sand more orange.

A has a loud saturated yellow ground against a rich orange-red barrel, matching the real cards' high-chroma backgrounds, while B's pale blue and beige surround is muted and leaves the barrel as the only color.
A's body is a deeper green with darker green shadows and a deeper crimson ground, closer to the real card than B's flatter green with an added brown base.
B's fins are a clean yellow with only a thin orange edge like the real fins, while A pushes a heavy orange rim.
A's sky, rails and body color are a little louder and more saturated like the real cards, while B's desert is dustier and greyer.
Both pair a yellow-lime ground with a bright orange rim, whereas the real card has a cooler minty green and a deeper red-orange rim, so color gives no reason to choose.
B's darker stripes lean slightly truer green, while A's lime-yellow top is warmer than the real minty green.
